key_impacts: Magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck offshore east of Sendai
All six external power lines to the plant were destroyed by the earthquake
evidence_snippets: On March 11, 2011, Japan was struck by a magnitude 9.0 earthquake centered 80 km east of Sendai.
The quake set a powerful tsunami in motion.
All six external power lines to the plant were destroyed by the earthquake.
missing_information: Casualties and damage scope across Japan

key_impacts: Station inundated by a series of tsunami waves ~45 minutes after the earthquake
Sea water pumps destroyed; cooling water unavailable
Complete loss of AC power (station blackout) for units 1–5
Batteries in units 1 and 2 were flooded and inoperable
evidence_snippets: About forty-five minutes after the earthquake, the station was inundated by a series of tsunami waves.
The tsunami destroyed the sea water pumps; 11 of 12 diesel generators failed.
This resulted in the complete loss of AC power for units 1–5; batteries in 1 and 2 were flooded.
missing_information: Tsunami wave heights at the site
